transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-13
- Start: 16:00 PST
- Duration: 56 minutes
- Recording: yes (auto)
- Attendees (shown): Maya Patel (AE) - Redwood, Liam Ortega (SE) - Redwood, Alex Chen - Peregrine, Sofia Alvarez - Peregrine, Daniel Park - Peregrine, Priya Rao - Peregrine

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Peregrine wants to see per-path (endpoint) usage analytics and a billing decomposition for LLM inference. They asked about mapping API routes to cost centers, support for tags, VPC/private deployment considerations, KMS/encryption, and Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization). AE and SE demo the Console per-path dashboards, cost-breakdown visualizations, and a mock chargeback/export to show FinOps alignment. Next steps include pricing, security docs, pilot scoping, and benchmark scripts.

Transcript (timestamps approximate, auto-timestamps every ~30s):
[00:00] Maya (AE): All right hello everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the account lead, and with me is Liam Ortega, our solution engineer. How's everybody doing?
[00:05] Alex Chen: Hey Maya, doing well, thanks. We got the product folks and finance on the line so I'll let folks intro quickly.
[00:09] Sofia Alvarez: Hi Sofia A., product eng at Peregrine.
[00:12] Daniel Park: Daniel Park, FinOps.
[00:14] Priya Rao: Priya, SRE. Running the k8s stuff.
[00:17] Maya (AE): Great. Quick agenda — show per-path usage dashboards, drill into cost breakdown per endpoint, talk about tagging and mapping to internal chargebacks, run through Optimize recommendations (batching/quant), and then Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:26] Alex Chen: Yep, sounds good. Main goal for us is to understand how to reliably map API routes and product features to our cost centers and identify where the biggest spend is. Also want to see what the console can actually export to our billing system.
[00:36] Liam (SE): Great. I'm going to share my screen and jump into the Console. Quick note — some of the labels in the export can be customized, and we'll show how tags propagate from API tokens through routes to the cost UI.
[00:45] [screen share starts]
[00:48] Liam (SE): Okay, this is the top-level Usage page. You can change the time window here, select granularity, and there's a per-path breakdown widget down here. I'm going to filter to the last 30 days.
[00:58] Sofia Alvarez: Can you show how you define a "path"? In our stack it's basically a combination of service name + route + model config.
[01:05] Liam (SE): Yep, good question. We treat a path as the route key your service sends — you can include multiple metadata fields: route name, model id, model variant, and we also support customer tags like product_area or team. So you can roll up by any of those dimensions.
[01:18] [00:01:20] Daniel Park: How accurate is the token-level attribution? We need it to be precise to within a few percent for chargebacks.
[01:26] Liam (SE): The console computes per-token CPU/GPU cost using our runtime's token accounting. For most inference modes we estimate cost per token with kernel-level profiling data and then attribute by path. There's a small margin for quantization differences, but typically within 3-5% of on-cluster benchmarking. We'll include the raw token counts if you'd rather recompute with your internal cost model.
[01:43] [00:01:44] Alex Chen: Do you have an example export that maps tokens to our internal GL code?
[01:48] Liam (SE): Yes — exports can include custom tags and a route id. You can push a CSV or S3 export daily or stream events to our billing webhook. For the demo I'll export a mock CSV so you can see columns.
[01:59] [00:02:00] [exports mock CSV shown]
[02:03] Sofia Alvarez: Nice, I see model_name, path_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_p50, latency_p95, cost_estimate, and custom_tag columns.
[02:10] Liam (SE): Exactly. You can map custom_tag to your GL code.
[02:14] [00:02:20] Maya (AE): A quick interjection — Daniel, for finance, we also support daily snapshots and a chargeback API that will surface line-items by path for ingestion into a billing system.
[02:27] Daniel Park: Good. We need the line items to reconcile with our monthly invoice.
[02:30] Liam (SE): We'll walk through the billing UI now. This is the Cost Breakdown page — it shows total spend and then a per-path bar chart. You can select a path and see a drill mode with token distribution and latency distribution side-by-side.
[02:42] [00:02:43] Sofia Alvarez: Can we show an example with a noisy endpoint — like our "variant-annotate" path that spikes tokens?
[02:49] Liam (SE): Sure, searching for variant-annotate... here it is. You can see a spike on Nov 3rd, token mix heavily skewed to long-context calls. We surface the average context length and persistent KV cache hit rate — that's useful for seeing if you can re-use cache and reduce cost.
[03:06] [00:03:07] Alex Chen: That KV cache metric is interesting. How does Redwood measure cache hits if we run Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:14] Liam (SE): For Hosted, it's measured inside our runtime and shown in the dashboard. For Dedicated, we ship the same telemetry agent and it emits stats back to your console aggregation endpoint, or you can keep telemetry private and run the report inside your VPC. In either mode, the instrumentation is consistent.
[03:28] [00:03:29] Priya Rao: On Dedicated, how much of the telemetry is PII or payload? We can't send full prompts.
[03:36] Liam (SE): We never send full prompt text by default. Telemetry is token counts, hash-based fingerprints, and metadata. If you want local-only telemetry we can support that with the Private deployment, or you can opt-in to sanitized traces.
[03:48] [00:03:49] Alex Chen: Okay good. Next, can we see the Optimize recommendations? We want to know where batching or quantization would save us the most.
[03:57] Liam (SE): Toggle to Optimize -> Workload Recommendations. This page runs heuristics across the path profiles — CPU/GPU per-token cost, latency distribution, and sequence length distribution. Here's a prioritized list: top candidate is "variant-annotate" — recommend float16 + dynamic batching window of 30ms, estimated 18% cost reduction with <5% latency tail impact.
[04:19] Sofia Alvarez: 30ms dynamic batching — would that impact real-time UX for our annotator? It's near-interactive.
[04:26] Liam (SE): Good call. The recommendation includes the expected added p50/p95. For this path p50 latency increases by ~8ms and p95 by ~60ms in the worst cases. If you require strict p95 SLO we can instead propose KV cache tuning or offloading longer-context jobs to a background route with cheaper model.
[04:45] [00:04:46] Daniel Park: Are those cost numbers model-agnostic? We use a mix of open LLMs and a proprietary fine-tuned on-prem model.
[04:53] Liam (SE): The Optimize engine uses the selected model profile. If you plug in your on-prem model profile (we have a profiler for that) it will recompute savings. For mixed fleet we support model routing and will show combined impact per path.
[05:06] [00:05:07] Alex Chen: Something we wrestle with: we have feature flags that route to different model versions; will the dashboard break out per-version or roll everything into the same path?
[05:16] Liam (SE): You can break out by model_version or roll up to path_id. It's flexible. Many teams keep per-version granularity during rollouts to catch regressions.
[05:25] [00:05:26] Maya (AE): Quick product note — we also support automatic fallback policies in routing. If a heavy model is unavailable, requests can fall back to a cheaper variant automatically and that fallback is tracked in the cost reports.
[05:38] Priya Rao: On security, we need SSO/SAML and RBAC for viewing the cost dashboards. Is that supported?
[05:45] Maya (AE): Yes — Console supports SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. You can limit access to cost exports at the role level so only finance gets CSV exports.
[05:55] [00:05:56] Alex Chen: Also KMS — we use an HSM-backed KMS. How does Redwood handle customer-managed keys for logs and for model artifacts?
[06:04] Liam (SE): For Private and Dedicated we integrate with your KMS/HSM for key wrapping of persistent logs and model snapshot encryption. For Hosted we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in supported clouds. We can send the integration how-to in the security pack.
[06:18] [00:06:19] Sofia Alvarez: Can you demo a sample daily export being ingested into an external system?
[06:25] Liam (SE): Sure — I set up a mock webhook sink. I'll trigger a manual export for the last 7 days.
[06:31] [export triggered]
[06:33] Liam (SE): The webhook receives a JSON payload with daily lines: path_id, team_tag, tokens_total, cost_estimate_usd, avg_context_len, cache_hit_percent. You can map team_tag to your GL account.
[06:46] Daniel Park: We also prefer S3 daily deltas for reconciliation. Is that supported?
[06:50] Liam (SE): Yep S3, BigQuery, or webhook streaming are all supported. We'll provide sample CloudFormation/Terraform to wire to your reconciliation pipeline.
[06:59] [00:07:00] Alex Chen: Let's talk about spike detection and anomaly alerts. We had a surprise run-away job last quarter. Can the Console alert on unusual token growth per path?
[07:09] Liam (SE): Yes — there's an alerts engine. You can create an alert: path token growth > 200% 24h or cost increase > $X/day. Alerts support slack/email/webhook. They can also trigger a policy to reduce concurrency on a given route temporarily.
[07:23] Priya Rao: Is that throttling per-route or global? We need per-route throttles for safety.
[07:28] Liam (SE): Per-route throttles are supported and can be automated through a policy.
[07:32] [00:07:33] Sofia Alvarez: A question about attribution: for multi-tenant paths where a single route serves multiple customers, can we break down cost by sub-customer or tenant id?
[07:43] Liam (SE): If you pass tenant_id as a tag on the request we will break it down; otherwise we can approximate based on request identifiers. Exact attribution requires the tag.
[07:51] Alex Chen: Ok that's important — we'll need to instrument tenant tags in our client wrapper.
[07:55] Maya (AE): Liam, demo the chargeback sample report exported to CSV and how to map fields to GL.
[08:02] Liam (SE): Export CSV done. Open file... you get line items per day per path. There's a column "charge_code" where you can put GL mapping. We also support a transform script on export if you want to programmatically map fields.
[08:15] [00:08:16] Daniel Park: Can you compute a projected monthly spend if we applied Optimize recommendations on the top 5 paths?
[08:23] Liam (SE): Yep — there's a projection mode. Selecting top 5 and applying the recommended config shows a projected $24k -> $19.6k monthly reduction (approx 18%). This assumes the same traffic profile.
[08:36] Sofia Alvarez: Nice. Does that projection account for the cost of additional instances needed to keep latency SLOs with batching?
[08:42] Liam (SE): It factors additional instance hours if needed; Optimize tries to find net savings including compute/throughput changes. It won't account for unrelated infra costs outside Redwood.
[08:55] [00:08:56] Alex Chen: Quick practical: If we want to run a pilot, what's the minimum data footprint and how long would we need to test?
[09:04] Maya (AE): For a representative pilot, 2 weeks of traffic on your top paths is usually enough to validate cost and latency tradeoffs. We recommend instrumenting tags and sending 14 days of history, then running Optimize for recommendations.
[09:16] Alex Chen: Who would be our direct Redwood contacts for the pilot?
[09:19] Maya (AE): I'll be the AE and coordinate. Liam will lead technical onboarding and bench runs. We'll loop our support engineer for Dedicated provisioning if needed.
[09:27] [00:09:28] Daniel Park: One last item — compliance. We'll need SOC2 Type 2 evidence and a reviewer call.
[09:33] Maya (AE): We have the SOC2 pack and an engineering security reviewer available next week. I'll include docs in the security pack.
[09:39] Priya Rao: For the private deployment option, are there networking diagrams? We need to show network egress and inbound rules.
[09:46] Liam (SE): Yes, the security pack includes network diagrams, VPC peering, and on-prem connector patterns.
[09:52] [00:09:53] Alex Chen: Ok thanks. Any other questions?
[09:56] Sofia Alvarez: One micro-question — can we annotate a path manually in the UI to mark it as "background-job" so it gets priced differently or excluded from SLO alerts?
[10:04] Liam (SE): Yes you can set path-level metadata including workload type; that filters in the cost views and alert rules.
[10:11] Maya (AE): Cool — wrapping up, I'll send the pilot pricing and security docs. Liam will attach benchmark scripts. Alex, you and Sofia will share the 15 endpoint list and tags. Daniel will review pricing with us.
[10:22] Alex Chen: Sounds like a plan. Thanks team.
[10:25] Daniel Park: Thanks.
[10:26] [closing remarks and sign off]
